I am 64 now, been working this land for 40 years. My 7.5 mu in Quzhou is mostly cotton — that's what I know best, and the soil here suits it. Stevia I planted on a small piece because the contract company came two years ago and the price was decent, but cotton is still my main thing.

For cotton, last year I got about 280 jin of lint per mu (around 140 kg). This year I will plant the same Bt hybrid seed I bought from the dealer in town — Lumianyan type, resistant to bollworm so I spray less. About 6 mu of cotton.

For fertilizer on cotton, I follow what I did last year because it worked. Before plowing I spread compound fertilizer 15-15-15, about 50 kg per mu as base. Then at squaring I topdress urea, around 20 kg per mu. At flowering another 15 kg of urea. So total nitrogen comes to roughly 23-24 kg per mu. Phosphorus and potassium each about 7-8 kg per mu from the compound. Potassium I add a bit extra at flowering, maybe 5 kg potassium sulfate, because cotton needs it for boll filling.

I plough deep before planting, then rotary to break clods. Cotton needs loose soil for the roots.

Irrigation — I have my own well, thank god. Cotton I water maybe 4 times: once after sowing if dry, then at squaring, flowering, and boll-filling. We had a dry spring last year so I watered 5 times.

Pesticide — even with Bt seed I still spray for aphids, spider mites, and lygus bugs. Maybe 6-7 sprays through the season. Plus topping the plants in late July and a growth regulator (mepiquat chloride) 2-3 times to control height.

Stevia on the other 1.5 mu — I transplant seedlings in April, harvest leaves twice. Less fertilizer than cotton, maybe 12 kg N, 5 kg P, 8 kg K. Water more often because shallow roots, maybe 6 times. Few sprays, just for leaf miners.
